name: web

scripts.test: ng test hub && ng test runner && ng test fleet
scripts.typecheck: npm run build && npm run typecheck:fleet
scripts.build: npm run build:hub && npm run build:runner
scripts.generate:client: openapi-ts -f openapi-ts.hub.config.ts && openapi-ts -f openapi-ts.runner.config.ts && node scripts/generate-stub-operations.mjs
scripts.story-render: tsc --noEmit -p projects/fleet/.storybook/tsconfig.json && npm run storybook:build && node scripts/story-render-check.js

//: vite is a direct devDependency, pinned to the exact version @angular/build depends on, because fleet/.storybook/main.ts imports mergeConfig from it and a different pin would install a second nested copy. npm's resolver cannot add some dependency sets under strict peer checking, because it walks optional peers (analog -> @angular-devkit/build-angular -> @angular/localize -> exact @angular/compiler-cli), so the next change to them must resolve the lock once with --legacy-peer-deps, never commit that setting, and re-prove that a strict npm install leaves package-lock.json unchanged and a strict npm ci passes. The overrides entry pins js-yaml to 4.3.2, the release that fixes all three of its advisories, because @hey-api/json-schema-ref-parser pins 4.2.0 exactly and npm's only offer is a downgrade of @hey-api/openapi-ts; codegen reads only our own openapi/*.openapi.json, so it is hygiene, and it goes once @hey-api's pin moves past 4.3.1.
